methodology.ew_slot_verification: Sampled 10 seed items across both packs (P1-EC-004, P1-EC-008, P1-EC-020, P1-ED-001, P1-ED-014, plus archived-reference items for pattern analysis). Confirmed EW empty-slot counts via direct file read. Extrapolated pattern across remaining 33 seeds using block-level heuristics consistent with the clone-rotation template structure.
methodology.p1_p2_split_rule: P1 = items with exactly 2 empty EW slots (i.e., 1 non-CC EW slot populated in addition to the required CC-empty). P2 = items with 3 empty EW slots (CC-empty + 2 non-CC slots empty, only 1 non-CC slot populated). This split is based on the observation that template-generated items either left 2 or 3 slots empty depending on rotation position.
methodology.estimated_effort_per_item: P1 items: 45-60 min each (1-2 non-CC EW authored + EC expansion). P2 items: 75-100 min each (2-3 non-CC EW authored + EC expansion). Both tiers share EC expansion, LOSTag recalibration, stem/distractor rewrite, and metadata calibration.

p0_blocking.why_this_blocks_seeds: Until all 33 clone-group replacements are production-inserted, the Domain E modernization denominator is unstable. Seed certification increments a numerator that should not be counted against an incomplete replacement baseline. Additionally, several seeds cover the same LOs as Wave 2b replacements — certifying seeds before replacements creates redundant effort and potential LO coverage double-counting.

estimated_total_effort.note: P2 items in block-4 (deepest in both packs: P1-EC-050 through P1-EC-072 and P1-ED-056 through P1-ED-075, 15 of 19 P2 items) show the most extreme template pattern. cross_pack_deduplication_warning.severity: HIGH — must precede any seed certification
cross_pack_deduplication_warning.issue: Pack C and Pack D Domain E items were generated from the SAME clone-rotation template. Both packs use identical topic sequences, identical MicroTopic strings, and identical UniqueConceptKey patterns (E-C### vs E-D###). The only differences are company-name rotation (Ashford/Emberton/Ironvale/Bramblewood vs. alternate names) and CorrectChoice letter rotation. A Pack C seed and its Pack D counterpart for the same topic are likely conceptual clones of each other.
evidence: P1-EC-004 (Pack C, segregation of duties, CC=A) and P1-ED-001 (Pack D, three lines model, CC=B) are different topics but generated by the same template engine.
P1-ED-014 (Pack D, independent verification, CC=D) and P1-EC-019/P1-EC-020 (Pack C, physical controls, CC=D) share identical 3-empty EW patterns from the same template.

The clone-group replacement program (R01-R40) treats Pack C and Pack D clones as a single pool — replacement item R09 replaces P1-ED-001 through P1-ED-005 (Pack D), while R01 replaces P1-EC-001 through P1-EC-005 (Pack C). The replacement program's architecture confirms cross-pack symmetry.
SESSION318_CLONE_GROUP_CLOSURE_AUDIT.json: '33 clone groups (each a 5-clone group from Pack C P1-EC-xxx or Pack D P1-ED-xxx)' — the program already models Pack C/D as interchangeable clone sources.
cross_pack_deduplication_warning.risk: If Pack C and Pack D seeds are certified independently without cross-reference, up to 19 of the 38 seeds may be cross-pack conceptual duplicates (same topic, different company name). This would waste 9-12 sessions certifying items that are clones of each other.
cross_pack_deduplication_warning.recommended_action: Execute cross-pack deduplication audit BEFORE any seed certification. Compare each P1-EC-XXX seed against its P1-ED-XXX counterpart (where XXX represents the same topic slot). If they test the same concept with only cosmetic differences (company name, CC letter rotation), consolidate to a single seed per topic. Expected outcome: 19 unique topics → ~12-15 unique seeds after dedup (some topics may genuinely differ). This could reduce total seed certification workload from 38 to 19-25 items.

lostag_calibration_requirement.current_state: All 38 seed items use LOSTag='E Internal controls' with no sub-tag granularity. This makes it impossible to verify blueprint coverage distribution — all items map to the same coarse bucket.
lostag_calibration_requirement.required_target: Fine-grained sub-tags per the Pack B Section E benchmark distribution: E.1.a through E.1.i. Pack B Section E (75/75 Certified) provides the distribution target. Each seed must be mapped to exactly one sub-tag based on its Topic/MicroTopic/UniqueConceptKey.

lostag_calibration_requirement.calibration_method: Map each seed's Topic and MicroTopic to the corresponding fine-grained LOSTag. Use Pack B Section E as the reference distribution. For seeds whose topic spans multiple sub-tags, assign the primary sub-tag and note the secondary coverage.
lostag_calibration_requirement.estimated_effort: 30-60 minutes total across all 38 items (included in per-item remediation estimates above).

session_estimates_summary.comparison_to_prior_estimate: SESSION318_SEED_INVENTORY.json estimated 9-12 sessions for seed certification alone. This prioritization refines that to 5-8 sessions for seeds (P1+P2) plus 1 session for P0 insertion and 1 session for dedup audit, total 7-10 sessions. The reduction is due to tiered prioritization (P1 items are significantly faster than the uniform per-item estimate) and the expectation that dedup will reduce total seed count.

assumptions_and_caveats: EW empty-slot counts are CONFIRMED for 5 seeds (P1-EC-004, P1-EC-008, P1-EC-020, P1-ED-001, P1-ED-014) via direct file read. Counts for the remaining 33 seeds are INFERRED from block-level heuristics. A full per-item EW audit (reading all 38 items' EW slots from source files) would replace inferred counts with confirmed counts but is estimated at 30-45 minutes of additional verification effort.

The P1/P2 split of 19/19 (exactly even) is based on the observed distribution: block-1 and block-2 items trend toward 2 empties (P1), block-3 and block-4 items trend toward 3 empties (P2). The actual split may be 17/21 or 20/18. The prioritization framework is robust to a ±3 shift.

The cross-pack dedup assumption (that Pack C and Pack D used the same template) is strongly supported by the clone replacement program architecture (33 groups spanning both packs), the identical MicroTopic/UniqueConceptKey patterns, and the symmetric archival patterns (56 archived + 19 retained in each pack). Formal confirmation requires item-by-item comparison.

P2 items in block-4 (P1-EC-050 through P1-EC-072, P1-ED-056 through P1-ED-075) may be the most template-damaged items in the seed pool. The cost-benefit of remediation vs. replacement should be evaluated before certifying these items. If 3 EW slots + EC + stem all need full rewrite, replacement may be more cost-effective and produce higher-quality items.

The LOSTag calibration assumes Pack B Section E distribution as the benchmark. If Pack B's LOSTag distribution is itself coarse (unlikely given its Certified/Gold Standard status), an alternative distribution target would be needed.
Session estimates assume current throughput of 7-10 items/session for P1 and 5-7 items/session for P2. Throughput may increase as the team gains familiarity with the seed remediation patterns.

This report does not address the 43 replacement items tracked in the Domain E modernization program. It covers only the 38 seed items from Packs C/D. The full Domain E certification workload is 81 items (38 seeds + 43 replacements).

The report priority ordering within P1 and P2 sorts by estimated effort (ascending). Within a given effort band, Pack C items are listed before Pack D items and lower block numbers before higher block numbers.
